notes: JUDGEMENT (recorded): boundary_seeds honest v1 signature. The packet quotes boundary_seeds(p: &dyn CertifiedPatch, q: &dyn CertifiedPatch) -> Construction<Vec<PointCert>>, but two frozen-seam facts make that spelling unrealizable: the R8 residual is arity 3, so its C1 certificate is the frozen arity-3 PointCert3 (PointCert.box_ is an IBox2 and cannot record an R8 box), and the R8 residual consumes a CONCRETE BezierLeaf homogeneous net (a &dyn CertifiedPatch cannot expose one). The landed v1 shape is boundary_seeds(p: &BezierLeaf, p_edges: &[BezierLeaf1], q: &BezierLeaf, q_edges: &[BezierLeaf1]) -> Construction<Vec<PointCert3>>, solving every edge of p against q and every edge of q against p as an R8 problem. Consistent with the packet's own honest scope, the edge set is CALLER-SUPPLIED (curve, chart) leaf data; the tests build the four leaf boundary curves from the public control nets. R8-stamped PointCert3 rebuilt through the documented one-line seam (PointCert3::try_new(ResidualId::R8, box_, rho)).

JUDGEMENT (recorded): Tier-1 margin derivation. The cos-space test bounds d.(n1 x n2) for the candidate d = (a1 x a2)/|a1 x a2| via the Lagrange identity (a1 x a2).(n1 x n2) = c1 c2 (1-m^2) - m c1 s2 (a1.r2) - m c2 s1 (a2.r1) - s1 s2 (a1.r2)(a2.r1) with n_i = c_i a_i + s_i r_i. Each factor is enclosed by a certified superset range: c_i in [cos_lb(theta_i), 1] with cos_lb = 1 - theta^2/2 rounded downward, s_i in [-min(theta_i,1), +min(theta_i,1)], m from an outward-rounded axis dot, and (a1.r2),(a2.r1) in [-sg_hi, sg_hi] with sg_hi the outward sqrt of the certified (1-m^2) range. The four terms are combined with outward-rounded interval arithmetic so the resulting lo is a certified lower bound of d.(n1 x n2); min_dot = g_lb/sg_hi, Proven iff it clears the TOL_JACOBIAN floor. This is a pure polynomial/trig-free inequality on the stored axis/half-angle data (NO angle function anywhere).

JUDGEMENT (recorded): fixture crossing parameters are non-dyadic by construction. A certified C1 requires the Krawczyk image STRICTLY inside the box, so a root whose parameter coordinate is an exact dyadic rational (e.g. 1/4) lies on a bisection boundary of the subdivision tree at depth >= 2 and can never certify. The single-crossing fixture uses the line C(t) = (1/5 + 7t/10, 1/5 + t/2, -1 + 3t), which pierces the plane z=0 at the non-dyadic product-space point (t,u,v) = (1/3, 13/30, 11/30), and the wavy-arch completeness fixture places the arch heights at 3/10 and 7/10 with arch roots at u ~ 1/3 and 2/3 so every crossing coordinate avoids the dyadic grid; both fixtures certify cleanly and the oracle count (1 and 4 seeds respectively) is reproduced exactly.

The dyadic-root hazard also explains why the completeness oracle passes exactly 4: the arch's u-boundary edges (constant height 0.2) never cross the plane and are pruned by the certified residual-exclusion at the root cell, and the plane's own edges against the arch produce no hits inside the arch domain; all 4 seeds are distinct transverse R8 certificates with rho <= RHO_MAX.
